did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel gives an exact date for the encounter: on the tenth day of the fifth month, in the seventh year. On that day, the elders of Israel came to him to inquire of the LORD.
Did you know? The LORD does not answer the elders immediately. Instead, he commands Ezekiel to set before them the detestable practices of their ancestors and examine their conduct.
Did you know? The LORD’s speech emphasizes that Israel was chosen in Egypt, where he declared to them, “I am the LORD your God.”
Did you know? The land promised to Israel is described in chapter 20 as “a land flowing with milk and honey,” also called “the most beautiful of all lands.”
Did you know? The Sabbath is presented in the chapter as a sign between the LORD and Israel, meant to remind them that the LORD is the one who sanctifies them.
Did you know? Because of the rebellion of the wilderness generation, the LORD swore that he would not bring that generation into the Promised Land, even though he had brought them out of Egypt.
Did you know? The chapter describes how the Israelites defiled themselves through idolatry by passing every firstborn through the fire; this appears as part of Ezekiel’s rebuke of Israel’s practices.
Did you know? Israel wants to be “like the nations” and serve wood and stone, but the LORD declares that this will not happen.

Did you know? In the future, the LORD describes gathering Israel from the nations and bringing them to “the wilderness of the nations,” where they will be judged face to face, just as their ancestors were judged in the wilderness of Egypt.
Did you know? The chapter’s vision of restoration ends with worship of the LORD on his holy mountain, on the heights of Israel, where all the house of Israel will serve him and bring their offerings.
